title: How do you say no politely?
examples: How do I say no without being rude?

explain.say: Here is a secret: you are allowed to say no, and you can say it kindly. Look at the board. In the kind no group: no, thank you; not today; I would rather not.

explain.say: Now look at the unkind group: ew, no way; that is stupid; ignoring or laughing. These hurt feelings, even when you just mean no. Can you turn one into a kind no?

explain.say: Here are the steps. Say no clearly, with a kind face and voice. You can give a reason if you want, but look at the board: no is enough on its own. Did you know that?

steps.label: Give a reason?
steps.note: Only if you want to. No is enough.
steps.ask: Do I have to give a reason when I say no?

steps.label: Say it again
steps.note: If they push, repeat it or walk away.
steps.ask: What if they keep asking after I say no?

explain.say: Offer another idea, and if someone keeps pushing, say it again or walk away. Fantastic! Remember: if anyone pushes you to do something unsafe, saying no and telling a trusted adult is always right.

faq.q: Is it okay to say no to a friend?
faq.a: Yes. Good friends respect each other's no. You can still be friends and say no to an idea.
asks: Tell me about the Kind no

faq.q: Do I have to give a reason when I say no?
faq.a: No. A reason can be friendly, but no, thank you is enough on its own.
asks: Tell me about the Give a reason?

faq.q: What if they keep asking after I say no?
faq.a: Repeat it calmly: I said no, thank you. If they still push, walk away and tell a trusted adult if you need help.
asks: Tell me about the Say it again
My friend will not take no for an answer

faq.q: How do I say no without being rude?
faq.a: Use a calm voice and kind words, like no thanks, maybe another time, and offer a different idea if you like.
asks: Tell me about the Unkind no

faq.q: When is it really important to say no?
faq.a: When something feels unsafe, unkind or wrong, or someone asks you to keep a secret that worries you. Then say no, get away and tell a trusted adult.
asks: When should I always say no?

facts: Counsellors call saying what you want clearly and kindly "being assertive", which is different from being passive or aggressive.
Many child-safety programmes teach children that they always have the right to say no to anything that feels unsafe.

quiz.say: A friend asks you to play a game you do not like. Which is a kind no?

options.show: No thanks, but how about tag?
options.say: No thanks, but how about tag?

quiz.why: It says no kindly and offers another idea.

quiz.say: Do you always need a reason to say no?

options.show: Only if you are an adult
options.say: Only if you are an adult

quiz.why: A reason is optional; your no counts on its own.

wrong.0: You can give one if you want, but you do not have to.
